messages:
IncidentBot: [INCIDENT RESOLVED] R-2026-17 resolved. Root cause: unexpected KV-cache churn causing Redis CPU to spike; mitigation deployed (LRU tuning + temporary read replica). Pager alerted at 2026-03-15T14:03:52Z.
Marcus Li: oncall here. I confirmed: a small deployment with new cache invalidation logic caused repeated prefix misses, which triggered heavy eviction + background compaction on our redis cluster. Rolling back that deploy dropped CPU and latency returned to normal.
Marcus Li: timeline for ops notes:
- 14:03 UTC: first pager (latency > 99th)
- 14:06: verified redis CPU spike on rds-redis-3
- 14:08: rolled back cache change on canary
- 14:12: applied LRU param bump across cluster
- 14:18: monitored stable; no further elevated errors
- 14:22: declared mitigated
Alex W.: quick customer impact summary for CS: ~12 customers saw >2x P99 latencies. BrightApps (enterprise) observed 5 minutes of 5xxs between 14:05-14:10 — their retries succeeded after 14:11. No data loss.
Joanna (CS): starting draft customer note below — please flag anything to change. Want to send to affected accounts in next 90 minutes once we agree on wording and credit.
Joanna (CS): ```
Hi <CustomerName>,

We wanted to let you know about an incident earlier today (2026-03-15) that affected request latency to the Redwood API. Between approximately 14:03 and 14:22 UTC some requests experienced elevated latency and a subset of requests returned 5xx errors for a short period.

What happened: An internal cache invalidation change caused higher-than-expected eviction activity in our Redis layer, which in turn increased CPU on the primary Redis node. This caused slower request processing for affected requests.

What we did: Our on-call team rolled back the change and applied protective LRU tuning; the system returned to normal within ~20 minutes.

Impact: Some requests experienced higher latency; a small number of customers saw transient 5xx failures. No customer data was lost.

Next steps: We will run an RCA with the infra and runtime teams to harden the cache invalidation path and add pre-deploy checks to catch this pattern. We expect to share a brief RCA and remediation plan within 3 business days.

As a gesture of goodwill we propose a single-service credit equal to 10% of the affected day’s usage for customers who experienced an outage window > 3 minutes. If that’s acceptable we will include it in the message.

Best,
Redwood Customer Ops
```
Priya Nair: status page copy suggestion — short and explicit. Putting below. Please review:
Priya Nair: ```
Summary: Degraded performance due to Redis evictions caused by a cache invalidation change.
Impact: Elevated latencies and transient 5xx errors for a subset of customers between 14:03–14:22 UTC.
Current status: Mitigated. Full service restored.
Next steps: RCA and code-level mitigation planned; timeline expected within 3 business days.
```
Marcus Li: added ops action items for the RCA — tagging infra-eng and runtime: wird: (cc @runtime-team).
Marcus Li: immediate tech action items:
- Add a canary-only stress test for cache invalidations in CI
- Add dashboard alert for eviction rate spikes (threshold: >500 evictions/min)
- Add a predeploy lint that warns on broad-invalidation changes
Alex W.: CS ask: please confirm the proposed credit and the eligibility criteria. Also need exact customer list (Joanna can you export last 2 hours of request logs for those with >3m error windows).
Joanna (CS): got it — exporting now, will share list in a follow-up DM and attach to the customer email send sheet.
Elena - CS Manager: 10% credit approval sounds reasonable as interim; ops leads, please confirm if that’s ok to promise to customers now or if we need finance signoff.
Marcus Li: ops is ok with that band as a goodwill gesture. No long-term SLA change implied.
Samir O.: next oncall (handoff) here — taking the watch for the 1600–0000 UTC window. Marcus, handing off open actions: RCA owner (Marcus), statuspage edit (Priya), CS email send (Joanna). I’ll be available if anything regresses. :white_check_mark:
Marcus Li: thanks — leaving notes in the incident doc and tagging owners.
IncidentBot: Incident R-2026-17 — status changed to resolved by Marcus Li at 2026-03-15T14:22:31Z.
Joanna (CS): final note — I'll queue the customer messages as soon as we confirm the credit text. Draft will go to the affected list only; we will copy account managers for enterprise customers.
Priya Nair: I'll push the status page update once Joanna confirms the final sentence about credits. Draft posted in ops-docs.
Elena - CS Manager: thanks everyone — good cross-team coordination. Please add the full timeline and remediation tasks to the RCA doc so we can share an executive summary with BrightApps tomorrow morning.
Marcus Li: adding final RCA link to thread when ready. Will aim for a 48h RCA.
Joanna (CS): follow-up planned: customer messages sent within 90 minutes pending final approvals.
Samir O.: noted and standing by.
Joanna (CS): :wave: sending a quick heads-up DM to BrightApps AMs now to avoid surprises.
IncidentBot: note — automated post-incident survey will go out to the oncall rotation in 24h.
